advice: Experiment: change only the C-store block after the K loop in `Llibxsmm_440`, for both 32-row halves. The current code extracts horizontal slices from ZA0.S and ZA1.S into `z0–z15`, and from ZA2.S and ZA3.S into `z16–z31`, then stores each output row with two single-vector `ST1W` instructions. Test storing in 4-row groups: after extracting one four-register ZA slice group, immediately issue its eight row stores using the existing C row stride and column offsets, then extract the next group. Keep the four ZA accumulators, tile mapping, store instructions, and K loops unchanged. Hypothesis: consuming each extracted group immediately may reduce the time many Z registers remain live and alter store scheduling. This is unverified advice, not a measured fact.
risks: The current two halves use different ZA horizontal slices and C base pointers; a wrong group-to-row mapping can swap rows or leave output unwritten. Immediate stores may add dependencies and provide no gain. Check that all 64 rows in each 32-column panel are written once, preserve the complete BSD notice and SME state handling, then run the fixed correctness checks for n=512, general sizes, odd tails, and n<=0 at tolerance 0.002. Measure repeated paired controls with benchmark, compiler flags, thread count, power source, and settings unchanged; report spread without assigning a joint or noisy result to this change alone.
